# 1 Kings Chapter 9 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** When Solomon had finished building the LORD's temple, the royal palace, and everything else he had wanted to build,

**2** the LORD appeared to him a second time, as he had at Gibeon.

**3** The LORD said to him, "I have heard the prayer and plea you made before me. I have consecrated this temple you have built by placing my name there permanently. My eyes and my heart will always be there.

**4** As for you — if you walk before me as your father David did, with integrity and uprightness, doing everything I have commanded and keeping my decrees and laws,

**5** I will establish your royal dynasty over Israel forever, as I promised your father David when I said, 'You will always have a successor on the throne of Israel.'

**6** But if you or your descendants turn away from me, fail to keep my commands and decrees, and go off to serve and worship other gods,

**7** then I will cut Israel off from the land I have given them. I will reject this temple I have consecrated for my name. Israel will become an object of ridicule and scorn among all peoples.

**8** And this temple will become a pile of rubble. Everyone who passes by will be shocked and will whistle through their teeth, asking, 'Why has the LORD done this to this land and this temple?'

**9** And the answer will be: 'Because they abandoned the LORD their God, who brought their ancestors out of Egypt. They embraced other gods, worshiping and serving them. That is why the LORD brought all this disaster on them.'"

**10** At the end of the twenty years during which Solomon built the two buildings — the LORD's temple and the royal palace —

**11** King Solomon gave twenty towns in Galilee to King Hiram of Tyre, who had supplied him with all the cedar, cypress, and gold he wanted.

**12** But when Hiram traveled from Tyre to see the towns Solomon had given him, he was not pleased.

**13** "What kind of towns are these you've given me, brother?" he said. He called the area Cabul — and the name has stuck to this day.

**14** Hiram had sent Solomon one hundred and twenty talents of gold.

**15** Here is an account of the labor force King Solomon conscripted for his building projects — the LORD's temple, the royal palace, the Millo, Jerusalem's wall, and the cities of Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer.

**16** Pharaoh king of Egypt had attacked and captured Gezer, burned it down, killed its Canaanite inhabitants, and given the city to his daughter as a wedding gift when she married Solomon.

**17** Solomon rebuilt Gezer, along with Lower Beth-horon,

**18** Baalath, and Tadmor in the desert,

**19** as well as all his storage cities, chariot cities, and cavalry cities — everything he wanted to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and throughout his realm.

**20** The surviving non-Israelite populations — descendants of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites —

**21** those the Israelites had been unable to destroy completely, Solomon conscripted as forced laborers. They remain so to this day.

**22** Solomon did not make slaves of any Israelites. Instead, they served as his soldiers, officials, commanders, captains, and chariot and cavalry officers.

**23** There were five hundred and fifty chief officers supervising Solomon's labor force.

**24** After Pharaoh's daughter moved from the City of David to the palace Solomon had built for her, he constructed the Millo.

**25** Three times a year Solomon offered burnt offerings and fellowship offerings on the altar he had built to the LORD, also burning incense before the LORD. So the temple was completed.

**26** King Solomon also built a fleet of ships at Ezion-geber, near Elath on the shore of the Red Sea in the land of Edom.

**27** Hiram sent experienced sailors from his own fleet to serve with Solomon's men.

**28** They sailed to Ophir and brought back 420 talents of gold for King Solomon.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

1. **9:3 — "my eyes and my heart"**: God's response to Solomon's prayer is startlingly intimate. He doesn't just consecrate a building — he commits his sustained attention and emotional investment to it. This is as close as the Hebrew Bible gets to saying God loves a place.

2. **9:6-9 — the temple's death sentence**: At the very moment of the temple's consecration, God describes its potential destruction. The most magnificent building in Israel's history comes with a built-in expiration clause: faithfulness, or ruin. The reader who knows the end of the story hears these verses differently.

3. **9:13 — Cabul**: The word likely means "good for nothing." Hiram's diplomatic insult is preserved in the text as a place name. International relations, even at their best, have friction.

4. **9:20-22 — forced labor, with a caveat**: Solomon conscripts non-Israelite populations but exempts Israelites from slavery. The distinction sounds principled, but 5:13 already told us Solomon conscripted 30,000 Israelites for rotating labor in Lebanon. The line between forced labor and non-slavery blurs under the weight of a building program this massive.

5. **9:28 — Ophir**: The gold of Ophir was legendary in the ancient world. Solomon's maritime expeditions, launched from the Red Sea port of Ezion-geber, represent the apex of Israelite commercial reach — and the beginning of dependence on international trade that will prove politically costly.

— PNEUMA
